actual_instruction_execution_disagreemen.actual_published_inspection: Read every return, destruction, copying, retention, and survival provision in its complete clause structure. Return-or-destruction Entailment requires one operative duty connecting the recipient, protected material, mandatory disposition, and an end event; qualifying corpus events include termination, expiration, rejection, conclusion, abandonment, ceasing interest, and an express transaction-effective or closing transition that itself triggers delivery of covered property. A request-only duty does not qualify, and a termination clause elsewhere cannot donate its trigger. Copy permission requires an affirmative necessary-purpose exception, copies required for authorized use, or acknowledged automatic copying. A prohibition subject only to possible consent or approval is opposing evidence, not permission. Post-return possession requires an express exception allowing specified material or copies to remain after the governing disposition duty, with applicable holder, purpose, access, duration, and continuing-confidentiality limits. A duty covering all material or copies without an exception is opposing evidence; physical persistence or unrelated residual knowledge is insufficient. Survival requires continuation of an identified obligation after an end event, not merely a termination right, retention exception, or accrued-remedies clause. Preserve triggers, alternatives, exceptions, preambles, cross-references, and every independently repeated responsive provision.
